claims.text: download manager remains stuck indefinitely in COMPLETE state if snapshot activation fails
claims.quote: If ActivateSnapshot fails, download manager is forever in COMPLETE state.

claims.text: a malicious peer can set data_length in utxosetinfo to an enormous value causing an immediate out-of-memory crash on the receiving node
claims.quote: Server can set `utxosetinfo`'s `data_length` field to 10 PB, which causes the receiving node to allocate >60 GB immediately.

claims.text: why invoke an RPC instead of a configuration option that could later be set by default
claims.quote: Why invoke an RPC, instead of a configuration option (which can be set by default at a later point)?

claims.text: why allow the user to specify block height when only hardcoded serialized hashes can be activated
claims.quote: Don't we only allow the specific hardcoded `CChainParams::m_assumeutxo_data::hash_serialized` to be activated? Then why allow the user to specify block height?

claims.text: introducing trust vectors and unvalidated UTXO blobs into the P2P network undermines trustless verification
claims.quote: One is free to add trust vectors to his own node implementation. Shoving that into the p2p network is not acceptable.
claims.status_note: author referred to mailing list replies in c:4468303593; evoskuil continued to oppose in c:4502401913 and subsequent comments
claims.status_by_quote: It has been anticipated for many years that degrading performance would lead to these exact calls to abandon validation.

claims.text: violates trustless verification by introducing a protocol-level dependency on hardcoded chainparams Merkle roots for accepting snapshots
claims.quote: This PR violates "don't trust, verify" by introducing a new protocol-level dependency on trusted, hardcoded data (Merkle roots in chainparams) for accepting a UTXO set snapshot from untrusted P2P peers.
claims.status_note: author in c:4468303593 deflected discussion to the mailing list without addressing the concern on GitHub

claims.text: dual chainstate complicates validation code paths across reorgs, rescanning, and pruning for a temporary security downgrade
claims.quote: the dual chainstate complicates every code path that touches validation - reorgs, wallet rescanning, pruning, the `*DANGER` suffixed methods.
claims.status_note: author replied in c:4468360424 asking for examples; l0rinc pushed back with detailed examples in c:4488453829 and reaffirmed Concept NACK in c:6095180069
claims.status_by_quote: My objection is that `assumeUTXO` makes the most critical part of the codebase harder to read and reason about, and this PR extends that model further.

claims.text: AssumeUTXO and multiple chainstates add excessive validation complexity for limited benefits that could be handled at higher layers
claims.quote: It adds a ton of validation complexity, and the benefits to me seem limited... Concept NACK any changes that add more AssumeUTXO complexity.
claims.status_note: author replied in c:4468360424; stickies-v pushed back in c:4479458931 citing PR 34521 and kernel decoupling issues
claims.status_by_quote: In my experience, many PRs involving validation logic are made more complex simply by having to reason about multiple chainstates

claims.text: snapshots could be fetched via https, ssh, ftps, or other encrypted mechanisms instead of adding P2P distribution
claims.quote: Even if true, it could easily be https/ssh/ftps or other encrypted internal mechanism, possibly even distributed.

claims.text: adds validation code complexity to the project for a low-priority feature
claims.quote: Concept NACK, for the same reasons @l0rinc has articulated very well

claims.text: incurs trust assumptions, implementation complexity, potential bugs, and data usage despite uncertain demand and adoption
claims.quote: this proposal comes with a bunch of concrete downsides: trust assumptions, implementation complexity leading to longer reviews and potential bugs, data usage.

claims.text: builds P2P distribution on top of an unsound AssumeUTXO foundation instead of prioritizing optimizations for full verification
claims.quote: AssumeUTXO is a bad proposal and adding the P2P mechanism on top of it is building on an unsound foundation.

claims.text: whether the node could determine snapshot height automatically in the future without requiring user input
claims.quote: do you think that in the future we could be smarter and decide the height by ourselves, without the user specifying it?

claims.text: whether AssumeUTXO with P2P sync but without background re-validation would be preferable
claims.quote: if we had the option of a assumeutxo *with* P2P sync, but *without* background re-validation, would that tilt the scales for commenters here, in one way or the other?
claims.status_note: fjahr rejected removing background re-validation in c:4530515268
claims.status_by_quote: I don’t find AssumeUTXO interesting if we don’t fully validate IBD in the background.

claims.text: how the trust model is affected when running alternate node implementations using the kernel lib
claims.quote: Would you feel the same way if the node software was from a different source? For example, it's now possible to run alternate node implementations using the kernel lib. And in such a case, what would your level of trust be then?
